body.txt: 1-Day Technology Update Workshop
AI Disruption and the Future of*Cooperative Enterprise Systems
Prepared for: ANGKASA IT Division (Bahagian Teknologi Maklumat)
Prepared by: red1
Facilitators: NUSA TEAM
Target Date: April 2026
Classification: Discussion Draft — For Internal Review
Executive Summary

ANGKASA sits at a critical juncture. Its core SPGA salary deduction system — serving 3.5 million cooperative members across 16,284 cooperatives — runs on Unisys ClearPath technology deployed since 1996. This 30-year-old mainframe backbone has been reliable, but the world around it is changing at unprecedented speed.

This paper presents the case that any ERP procurement exercise conducted in 2026 without accounting for AI disruption risks locking ANGKASA into another generation of vendor dependency — precisely at the moment when the economics of enterprise software are being fundamentally rewritten.

The opportunity is equally significant: ANGKASA’s unique position as the apex body for 16,284 cooperatives with RM165.8 billion in assets makes it an ideal incubator for a cooperative-owned technology platform that could serve the entire movement — at a fraction of proprietary costs.
Part 1: The FUD That Should Concern You
1.1 Your ERP RFP May Already Be Outdated

If ANGKASA is evaluating enterprise systems using a traditional RFP framework — comparing SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft on features, pricing, and implementation timelines — the evaluation criteria themselves may be obsolete within 18 months.
Why? Because the ERP market is undergoing its most significant disruption in 35 years:
“Through 2027, GenAI and AI agent use will create the first true challenge to mainstream productivity tools in 35 years, prompting a $58 billion market shake-up.”*— Gartner, 2025
Key data points your RFP evaluation may not have considered:
The risk: Selecting a vendor today based on 2024-era criteria means you are buying a system designed for the era that is ending, not the one beginning.
1.2 The SAP 2027 Cliff

SAP has set a hard deadline: mainstream ECC support ends December 31, 2027. Extended maintenance (to 2030) costs a 2% premium on top of the existing 22% maintenance fee. Organizations that wait face 30-50% higher consulting rates due to the global migration demand surge.
What this means for ANGKASA: Any vendor proposing SAP is proposing a system whose predecessor is being forcibly retired. The migration track record is sobering:
32% of companies migrating to S/4HANA have underestimated total cost
Typical migration: 12-24 months, often extending beyond
Organizations on unsupported ECC face 40-60% higher total cost of ownership
1.3 Oracle and Microsoft Are Raising Prices
The proprietary ERP vendors are coordinating price increases while bundling AI features that may or may not deliver value:

cell.txt: First price increase in 5 years (Nov 2025); M365 suite +8-23% effective (Jul 2026)

body.txt: At Oracle pricing, 100 ANGKASA staff = RM3.3 million/year in license fees alone. At SAP pricing, the same could exceed RM6.6 million/year.
This is before implementation, customisation, training, and ongoing support.
1.4 The AI-Native Disruption Is Real

In October 2025, a startup called DualEntry emerged from stealth with $90 million in funding (Lightspeed, Khosla Ventures, Google Ventures) and a provocative claim: they can migrate organisations off legacy ERP systems in 24 hours.
Their investor thesis was published under the title: "The Death of the Legacy ERP".
Key claims:
First ERP built from the ground up with AI (not AI bolted onto legacy code)
Already processed $100 billion in journal entries
Signed thousands of global users in months
Valued at $415 million in 15 months

Whether DualEntry succeeds is not the point. The point is that $100M+ in venture capital is betting that legacy ERP can be replaced by AI-native alternatives. This is a structural market shift, not a trend.
1.5 Forrester’s Warning on Vendor Lock-In
Forrester’s 2026 enterprise software predictions contain a specific warning:

“Consolidating to a primary platform concentrates risk and neuters negotiation leverage, making the next major software decision a bet on a single vendor’s security posture, pricing model, and innovation capacity for the next decade.”
“Vendors are using AI to drive new revenue streams while tightening control... The era of experimentation is over. The era of monetisation has begun.”

Translation: The vendors offering AI features are using them as a justification to raise prices and deepen lock-in. An RFP that selects a proprietary vendor today is not just buying software — it is accepting a decade of pricing decisions made by that vendor.
Part 2: The Strategic Position
2.1 ERP Vendor Landscape — Cost vs AI Readiness
The following matrix positions major ERP options on two axes that matter for ANGKASA’s decision:

cell.txt: OPPORTUNITY ZONE**Open Source + AI Layer*(iDempiere/ERPNext +* local AI integration)

body.txt: Reading the matrix:
Top-left quadrant (High Cost, High AI): SAP and Oracle are investing heavily in AI, but at extreme cost. ANGKASA would pay RM3-7M/year for 100 users and still be locked into their roadmap.
Bottom-right quadrant (Low Cost, Low AI): Open source ERP (iDempiere, ERPNext) costs almost nothing in licensing but has no native AI today.

The Opportunity Zone (center-right): An open-source ERP base enhanced with a targeted AI layer — built or integrated locally — combines low cost with relevant AI capability. This is where ANGKASA should position.
2.2 Deployment Strategy — Implementation Risk vs Cooperative Fit
This matrix evaluates deployment approaches against the unique requirements of a **federated cooperative movement**:

COOPERATIVE FIT* HIGH* |* | Cooperative iDempiere* | Tech Incubator Shared Platform* | (ANGKASA-owned) (OSGi modular)* |* | ERPNext* | (shared instance)* |* | Odoo Enterprise* |* | DualEntry MS Dynamics* | (fast but* | no coop SAP/Oracle* | model) (enterprise-only,* | no federation)* |* LOW* +---------------------------------->* HIGH IMPLEMENTATION LOW* RISK RISK RISK
Reading the matrix:
Bottom-left (High Risk, Low Fit): SAP/Oracle are designed for single enterprises, not federated cooperative movements. Implementation risk is extreme (12-24 months, cost overruns).

Top-right (Low Risk, High Fit): A cooperative-owned technology incubator using open-source ERP scores highest. Proven in the credit union sector (Velera serves 4,000 credit unions; CU*Answers is cooperative-owned core processing).

iDempiere sits in the best position for ANGKASA specifically: Java/OSGi modularity means each cooperative type can have custom plugins, it matches ANGKASA’s enterprise IT culture, and it has an active Malaysia community.
2.3 The Cost Reality at ANGKASA’s Scale
ANGKASA is not a single company. It is the technology backbone for 16,284 cooperatives and 7.22 million members. At this scale, vendor pricing models produce staggering numbers:
The question is not "Can ANGKASA afford SAP?" The question is: "Can 16,284 cooperatives justify sending RM80-160 million to a foreign vendor over 5 years when cooperative-owned alternatives exist?"
Part 3: ANGKASA as Technology Incubator
3.1 The Precedent: Credit Union Shared Services
The model already exists — not in theory, but in production at massive scale:
These are cooperatives building technology platforms for cooperatives. The members own the platform. The costs are shared. The vendor lock-in is zero.
ANGKASA already operates this way for salary deductions (SPGA). The question is: why not extend the model to ERP?
3.2 The ANGKASA Incubator Concept
3.3 Why iDempiere Fits ANGKASA

cell.txt: Matches ANGKASA’s existing IT culture (enterprise-grade, not startup-grade)
Each cooperative type gets purpose-built plugins without forking the core
Zero license fees. ANGKASA owns the code. No vendor can raise prices.
Redhuan D. Oon (author of Open Source ERP, Pearson Malaysia) is based in Putrajaya. Local expertise exists.
Modules for supply chain, warehousing, POS — relevant to diverse cooperative types
Built-in support for multiple entities sharing one database — ideal for cooperative federation

body.txt: 3.4 The AI Layer — Built, Not Bought
Rather than buying AI from SAP or Oracle (at their prices, on their terms), ANGKASA could build an AI capability layer on top of open-source ERP:

cell.txt: Agentic AI on structured ERP data
Monthly close, audit preparation, regulatory compliance
Housing cooperative design → BOM → cost estimate
AI on SPeKAR + cooperative financial data
Enhance loan assessment for cooperative members
AI agents replacing manual approval chains

body.txt: This is the "Opportunity Zone" from the strategy matrix — open source ERP + locally-built AI, owned by the cooperative movement.
Part 4: The DaKoM 2030 Alignment
Malaysia’s Dasar Koperasi Malaysia (DaKoM) 2030 targets:
Cooperative sector revenue of RM73 billion by 2030 (from RM45.5 billion)
Active cooperative rate of 65%
Improvement in Cooperative Member Well-being Index (IndeKA) to 80
A technology incubator directly supports all three targets:

cell.txt: Shared ERP reduces operational costs, freeing capital for growth. AI automation improves productivity.
Low-cost shared platform makes digital tools accessible to small and inactive cooperatives currently priced out.
Better financial management, faster loan processing, transparent reporting improve member well-being.

body.txt: Budget 2026 allocated RM50 million for cooperative development through SKM. A portion directed toward a cooperative technology incubator would have multiplied impact across all 16,284 cooperatives.
Part 5: Workshop Agenda
Morning — Understanding the Threat

cell.txt: Workshop objectives. Why this matters now.
Gartner’s 40% AI agent prediction. DualEntry and the "Death of Legacy ERP" thesis. What "AI-native" means vs "AI-bolted-on". Demo: AI agent processing a cooperative financial report.

SAP 2027 deadline. Oracle’s RM33K/user/year. Microsoft’s 23% effective increase. Forrester’s lock-in warning. Cost projections at ANGKASA’s scale. Interactive exercise: calculate your own 5-year TCO under three scenarios.

body.txt: Afternoon — Seeing the Opportunity

The cooperative technology incubator model. Architecture walkthrough. How OSGi

Module 6: The AI Layer You Can Own
Local AI deployment (not cloud-dependent). Document processing demo. BIM Compiler demo (housing cooperative use case). Financial reporting agent concept.
9-Quadrant SWOT analysis (Prof. Wan Mohtar’s methodology). Teams draft a 90-day action plan. Presentation and critique.
Summary of key decisions. Next steps. Commitment to action.

body.txt: Part 6: Recommended Next Steps for ANGKASA

cell.txt: Pause or reframe any active ERP RFP to include AI-readiness and cooperative-fit criteria
Commission a formal TCO comparison: proprietary vs open-source at ANGKASA scale
Pilot iDempiere with one cooperative type (e.g., credit cooperative) as proof of concept
Establish a Technology Incubator steering committee with representation from diverse cooperative types
Present incubator concept to SKM for alignment with DaKoM 2030 and Budget 2026 allocation
Develop HRDC-claimable training curriculum for cooperative digital readiness
